title: Normalized vector-bundle purity family
statement: The independently integration-normalized family exists and is invertible on every ordinary unbounded input, with the unique restricted purity isomorphism and coefficient-unit orientation.

source.place: paragraph 2; assembly step 3, normalized transpose in the published vector-purity coordinates

proof.text: The adopted finite-coefficient projection theorem isIso_projectionMap_of_finite makes the twist-first natural projection invertible. Define c as inverse projection followed by tensoring the integration trace and the left unitor. Transpose each component under the Brown adjunction. Naturality of c and homEquiv_naturality_left_square give a natural transformation gamma, and the adjunction inverse identity gives its counit equation. These are the construction and normalization in private normalized_of_iso_mates. Private normalized_etale_general specializes the categorical construction at the abstract coefficient-category interface, private normalized_finite_general then specializes to ModuleCat A while retaining the native ordinaryFiniteUnit target of the trace; the public proof substitutes the vector projection; this preserves all canonical functors and projection components.

Private swap_mate_isIso conjugates the coefficient-first counit by the canonical source braiding. Expand the coefficient-first projection, invert its three factors, cancel the source braiding, and use braiding naturality at the trace and braiding-unit compatibility to obtain exactly the twist-first counit c. Adjunction naturality identifies its adjunct with the source braiding followed by the established vectorIntegrationMate_isIso adjunct. Both factors are invertible. The finite-unit comparison hom is the identity by singleFunctorObjUnitIso_inv and hom_inv_id. This proves invertibility of gamma at every ordinary unbounded input.

Restrict the inverse of the natural isomorphism gamma to the constructible finite-Tor full subcategory. Its inverse has the required normalization. Any other normalized restricted isomorphism has the same inverse components: cancel the invertible projection, then apply injectivity of the adjunction Hom bijection. This proves the unique restricted purity family.

Let e be tensoring the pullback-unit comparison with W followed by the right unitor. The source-library projectionMap_rightUnitality gives projection at the unit followed by L(e.hom) equal to the right unitor. Invert this equation. Compose the unit component of gamma with e.inv and transpose: naturality of the right unitor and equality of the two unit unitors reduce the resulting counit to t. Thus inverse gamma at the unit followed by e is the required coefficient orientation. Injectivity of the same adjunction Hom bijection proves uniqueness of this orientation. All of this is a categorical calculation and does not impose any additional geometric, rank or coefficient hypothesis.
